clue.text: Ace crossword — no indication of alternative — cryptic? Such may be beyond criticism

indicators.note: cryptic means puzzling or obscure, so the letters of the phrase are to be jumbled
no says the letters of the following piece are absent from the jumbled pool

parts.note: the word 'or' is what signals an alternative in a sentence

explanation.surface: A solver wonders whether a top-class puzzle with no either/or choices counts as properly cryptic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cryptic' rearranges ACE CROSSWORD once 'no' has removed OR (the 'indication of alternative'), leaving ten letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Sacred cows are idiomatic institutions or beliefs held to be immune from criticism.

clue.text: Money going into the pockets of bad people?

definitions.text: Money going into the pockets of bad people?

parts.words: Money going into the pockets of bad people?
parts.note: reads like a remark about crooks' earnings, but 'bad' here means unwell: state money paid to those off work through illness

explanation.walkthrough: 'Bad' suggests wicked people; the other sense is 'poorly', as in feeling bad.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the payment made to employees unable to work through illness, so it goes to people who feel bad.

clue.text: China caught America mostly in disarray

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

indicators.note: something in disarray is jumbled, so these letters are rearranged
mostly means nearly all of the word, so its final letter is dropped

parts.note: the last letter of America

explanation.surface: A news headline: China has caught a disorganised America out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' trims America to AMERIC, and 'in disarray' rearranges that to ERAMIC after C. 'China' is not the country but porcelain.
explanation.definitionFit: China, meaning porcelain tableware, is a kind of ceramic ware.

clue.text: French are for one extended article

parts.note: es is the French for 'are' with tu, as in tu es
say, like 'for one', introduces an example

explanation.surface: A French person explaining that they are in favour of one long piece of writing.
explanation.definitionFit: An essay is a longer piece of writing on one subject, an extended written article.

clue.text: Certain Catholic King involved in tragedy

parts.note: Lear is the king at the centre of Shakespeare's tragedy King Lear

explanation.surface: A Catholic monarch caught up in some terrible event.
explanation.definitionFit: To be clear about something is to be certain of it, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Wayward ball and golf tournament's winnable by anyone

parts.note: in cricket a wide is a ball bowled out of the batter's reach
the Open is the British Open golf championship

explanation.surface: A sports report: wild shots mean the golf competition could go to anybody.
explanation.walkthrough: A wide is a cricket delivery too far from the batter to hit, so 'Wayward ball' is cricket, not golf.
explanation.definitionFit: A contest described as wide open has no clear favourite, so anybody could take it.

clue.text: Son engaged in reverse of best job

indicators.note: engaged in means held within, so the son's letter sits inside the other piece
reverse of means the word for best is read backwards

parts.note: top means best, as in top marks

explanation.surface: A son who has got involved in the opposite of the best job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reverse of' turns TOP into POT; 'engaged in' puts S inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A post is a position of employment, a synonym for a job.

clue.text: Some Americans noticed cut jewel being lifted

indicators.note: in a down answer, lifted means read upwards, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: saw means noticed

indicators.note: cut means the end is lopped off the word for jewel

parts.note: a bijou is a jewel or trinket
the last letter of bijou

explanation.surface: Some Americans spotted that a precious stone was being stolen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' trims BIJOU to BIJO; 'being lifted' reverses SAW BIJO to OJIBWAS. 'lifted' looks like stolen; in a down clue it means reversed.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ojibwas are a Native American people of the Great Lakes region.

clue.text: Draw canal upwards

indicators.note: in a down clue, upwards means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: gut is the alimentary canal

explanation.surface: An instruction to sketch a waterway going uphill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'canal' is the alimentary canal, not a waterway; 'upwards' reverses GUT.
explanation.definitionFit: To tug is to pull hard, and draw also means to pull.

clue.text: National border within confines of Asia — something abhorred

indicators.note: within means placed inside the other piece
the confines of a word are its outer limits, its first and last letters

parts.note: Nat is a standard abbreviation for national
a hem is the border of a piece of cloth

explanation.surface: A national frontier lying inside Asia is something hated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'within' is the container signal and 'confines of' keeps only the edge letters of Asia; 'border' is a sewn edge, not a frontier.
explanation.definitionFit: Anathema is a thing or person intensely loathed, so something abhorred.

clue.text: Vehicle maintenance left incomplete

indicators.note: left incomplete means the word for maintenance loses its last letter

parts.note: care means upkeep or maintenance
the final letter of care

explanation.surface: A vehicle whose servicing was abandoned half-done.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left incomplete' drops the E from CARE.
explanation.definitionFit: A car is a motor vehicle, the definition being its general class.

clue.text: Skilful footwork, pending cast changes

indicators.note: changes means the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A dancer's nimble feet while a reshuffle of the cast awaits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changes' rearranges PENDING CAST.
explanation.definitionFit: Step dancing is a style of dance built on intricate, precise steps.

clue.text: Ghastly party, no skill, very uneven

parts.note: bum is slang for bad or dreadful

indicators.note: no means the word for skill is taken out

parts.note: art is skill, as in the art of conversation

explanation.surface: A dreadful party with no talent on show, a very patchy affair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no' removes ART from party, leaving PY.
explanation.definitionFit: A bumpy surface or ride is very uneven, full of jolts.

clue.text: Part of church entrance knocked over by haulage expert?

indicators.note: knocked over means the word is turned round, read backwards

parts.note: a door is an entrance
a tower is something or someone that tows, hence a haulage expert, flagged by the question mark

explanation.surface: A truck driver smashes the doorway of a church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knocked over' turns DOOR into ROOD; TOWER is 'one who tows', not a tall building.
explanation.definitionFit: A rood tower is a church tower standing over the crossing, where the rood or cross is set.

clue.text: Medical organisation regarding councillor in decline

parts.note: re means regarding or concerning

indicators.note: in means placed inside the other piece

parts.note: a descent is a decline

explanation.surface: A health body discussing a local councillor's deterioration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is the container signal; 'decline' reads as a verb or fall in health but supplies a downward slope.
explanation.definitionFit: The Red Crescent is the counterpart of the Red Cross in Muslim countries, a humanitarian medical body.

clue.text: Woman backed fashionable drink

indicators.note: backed means the word is reversed

parts.note: in means fashionable, as in the in thing
cola is a soft drink

explanation.surface: A woman supported a trendy beverage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backed' reverses IN to give NI. 'backed' looks like 'supported' but signals reversal.
explanation.definitionFit: Nicola is a woman's given name.

clue.text: Lipid in blood and eggs — it's found in lichen, unexpectedly

indicators.note: unexpectedly suggests the letters turn up in a surprising order, so they are rearranged

parts.note: it, with the 's (is) joining it to what follows

explanation.surface: A biochemistry note: a fatty substance in blood and egg yolk turns up surprisingly in lichen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unexpectedly' rearranges IT and LICHEN; 'found in' links.
explanation.definitionFit: Lecithin is a fatty compound present in egg yolk and blood plasma, so a lipid.

clue.text: Backed poetry penned by radical

indicators.note: penned by means enclosed by, as in a pen

parts.note: red means politically radical or left-wing
verse is poetry

explanation.surface: Poems written by a revolutionary got support.
explanation.walkthrough: 'penned by' looks like 'written by' but means enclosed, as in a pen; 'Backed' means went backwards, not supported.
explanation.definitionFit: Backed and reversed both mean moved backwards, as a car is backed or reversed.

clue.text: One deception taking in sailor over a girl

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means placed above what follows

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: taking in means holding inside, so the sailor goes into the word for deception

parts.note: a sell is a hoax or deception
AB is an able seaman, a sailor

explanation.surface: One con trick involving a seaman put above a young woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking in' is the container signal; 'over' works because in a down answer the earlier part sits above the later.
explanation.definitionFit: Isabella is a woman's given name, so a girl's name.

clue.text: Expected outcome of returning with different actors

indicators.note: returning means the little word is read backwards

parts.note: a recast play has new performers

explanation.surface: What is likely to happen when a play comes back with a new cast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' reverses OF to FO. 'of' looks like a link word but is the piece being turned.
explanation.definitionFit: A forecast is a prediction, the result that is anticipated.

clue.text: Regret about key river salvage worker

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the word for regret goes round the key

parts.note: to rue is to regret
Esc is the escape key on a keyboard

explanation.surface: Sorrow over a crucial river recovery operative.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' is the container signal; 'key' looks like crucial but is a keyboard key.
explanation.definitionFit: A salvage worker saves people or goods from wrecks, so is one who rescues.

clue.text: Fairground worker and drink supplier not turning to go

indicators.note: not means the next piece is removed

parts.note: a barkeeper serves drinks

indicators.note: turning means the word is read backwards

parts.note: to go (to the toilet) is to pee

explanation.surface: A fairground hand and a barman who will not budge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning' makes EEP from PEE (the euphemism 'to go'), and 'not' takes it out of BARKEEPER.
explanation.definitionFit: A barker is the person outside a fairground show who calls to passers-by to come in.

clue.text: Some current on a line fed into outskirts of Kinshasa (African city)

indicators.note: fed into means inserted inside the other piece
the outskirts of a word are its first and last letters

parts.note: an amp is a unit of electric current, so some current

explanation.surface: Electric power on a cable supplied to the edge of the Congolese capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outskirts of' gives K and A; 'fed into' puts AMP, A, L between them. Kinshasa is a city too, but here only its edge letters count.
explanation.definitionFit: Kampala is the capital of Uganda, an African city.

clue.text: Glassware and barrels rolled over into river

indicators.note: into means placed inside the other piece

parts.note: the Tees is a river in north-east England

indicators.note: rolled over means turned round, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: butts are large casks or barrels

explanation.surface: Glass items and casks tumbling into a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rolled over' reverses the barrels to give STTUB, and 'into' puts that inside the river Tees of north-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: Test tubes are slim glass vessels used in laboratories, a kind of glassware.

clue.text: Indistinct sounds used to be observed after silence

indicators.note: after means this piece follows the one for silence

parts.note: sh is a call for silence
was means used to be

explanation.surface: Muffled noises that were once heard after a hush.
explanation.walkthrough: A schwa (also spelt shwa) is the neutral vowel sound in unstressed syllables, as in 'about'.
explanation.definitionFit: Shwas are the weak, unstressed vowel sounds of speech, so indistinct sounds.

clue.text: Anglophile US writer crowds around English

indicators.note: around means the word for crowds encloses the next piece

parts.note: jams means crowds or crams

explanation.surface: An American author who loved England is mobbed by English fans.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' puts JAMS round E.
explanation.definitionFit: Henry James was an American-born novelist who settled in England and took British citizenship.

clue.text: Judge's indignation seeing stripping person in courtroom

parts.note: J is the abbreviation for judge

indicators.note: stripping means the outer layer, here the first letter, is removed

parts.note: furor is angry indignation
the first letter of furor

explanation.surface: A judge is outraged to see someone undressing in court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stripping' removes the F from FUROR. 'stripping' looks like undressing, but it takes off the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A juror sits in the courtroom as a member of the jury.

clue.text: US state, not so mountainous, containing source of unique vegetable

indicators.note: containing means the state's letters enclose the next piece

parts.note: Calif is the abbreviation for California

indicators.note: the source of a word is its first letter

parts.note: lower means less high, not so mountainous

explanation.surface: A US state, less hilly, with a one-off vegetable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'source of' takes the first letter of unique and 'containing' puts it inside the state's short form; 'not so mountainous' comes last.
explanation.definitionFit: Cauliflower is a brassica eaten as a vegetable.

clue.text: Line not required for Arctic fish

indicators.note: not required means the letter for line is dropped

parts.note: Arctic means extremely cold

explanation.surface: A fishing line is not needed for a fish of polar waters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not required' removes L from COLD. 'Arctic' seems to describe the fish but is the word being cut.
explanation.definitionFit: Cod is a common food fish of the North Atlantic.

clue.text: Cut most of lines on graph

indicators.note: most of means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: axes are the reference lines of a graph
the final letter of axes

explanation.surface: Remove the majority of the lines plotted on a chart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most of' trims AXES.
explanation.definitionFit: To axe something is to cut it, as with a budget or a job.

clue.text: Unilluminated vessel on Dee

indicators.note: in an across clue, on means placed after

parts.note: dee is the spelt-out name of the letter D
an ark is a boat, as Noah's

explanation.surface: An unlit boat on the River Dee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dee' looks like the river but is the letter D, spelt out.
explanation.definitionFit: Dark and unilluminated both mean lacking light.

clue.text: Member of staff very gripped by tirade from minister?

parts.note: a minister lives in a manse, so it is where a minister comes from

indicators.note: gripped by means held inside the next piece

parts.note: a rant is a tirade

explanation.surface: A staff member is caught up in a minister's tirade.
explanation.walkthrough: A manse is a Scottish minister's house; 'gripped by' puts V inside RANT after it.
explanation.definitionFit: A manservant is a male domestic employee, a member of a household staff.
